findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never validates the grant shortcut (wrong offset + inverted condition)
findings.body:
The new matcher is supposed to assert that the access-token id has the form `<sessionType><tokenType><grantType>:<uuid>` with the expected grant shortcut. Two defects make it a no-op:

1. The grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 of the 6-char prefix (`substring(4, 6)`), not `substring(3, 5)`; for `onrtac:...` the code reads "ta" instead of "ac".
2. The comparison is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns a mismatch when the value *equals* the expected shortcut.

As a result every token id of the right shape passes regardless of the encoded grant type, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` silently stop verifying the feature introduced by this PR. The condition should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` (plus a length check on `items[0]` to avoid StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on unexpected ids).

findings.title: Copy-paste error: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`. A `null` raw token id therefore passes construction and only surfaces later: `encodeTokenId()` produces an id ending in the literal string "null" (e.g. `onrtac:null`), which would be used as the `jti` of a real access token. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, which is a documented extension point for custom grant types. Any third-party factory built against a previous release will fail to compile, and an already-built provider jar will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all grant factories and calls `getShortcut()` — i.e. the whole server fails to start. Consider providing a `default` implementation (e.g. returning the "unknown" shortcut) and handling it gracefully in the encoder factory, or at minimum document this as a breaking SPI change.

findings.title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed without deprecation
findings.body: The `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted in this change. `OAuth2GrantType` is an extension SPI, so any external grant-type implementation that wrapped/copied the context (a natural pattern for decorating contexts) will no longer compile against this version. If removal is required because the new `grantType` field cannot be derived in a copy, either keep the constructor and copy `grantType` too, or state the removal explicitly in the upgrading notes.

findings.title: Javadoc for getShortcut() says '3-letters' but the encoder requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc states the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", while all in-tree implementations return 2 characters and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` hard-requires the encoded prefix to be exactly 6 characters (2 for session type + 2 for token type + 2 for grant type). A custom grant type that follows the Javadoc and returns a 3-character shortcut would produce access-token ids that the very same provider cannot decode (`IllegalArgumentException: ... Expected length of 6`). The contract must state exactly 2 characters (and ideally be enforced).

findings.title: No validation of grant shortcut (null / wrong length) during postInit
findings.body: `postInit()` puts `gtf.getShortcut()` directly into a `ConcurrentHashMap`. If a (third-party) `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` returns `null`, `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)` throws a bare `NullPointerException` during `postInit`, aborting server startup with no indication of which provider is at fault. Similarly a shortcut whose length is not exactly 2 is accepted here but produces token ids that `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` rejects. Validate non-null and length==2 here with a message naming the offending factory, analogous to the existing duplicate-shortcut check.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the expected validation
findings.body: The test constructs the factory without calling `postInit()`, so `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory` is `null`. For the unknown shortcut "ac", `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` misses the map and dereferences `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, throwing a `NullPointerException`. Because the test catches the broad `RuntimeException`, it reports success while never exercising the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type")` path. Catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically (and assert its message), and make the fixture supply a non-null session factory so the refresh-on-miss code path is actually covered.

findings.title: Access-token jti format change is not documented in release/upgrading notes
findings.body: From this change on, every access token's `jti` (and the `token_id` event detail) is no longer a plain UUID but `<6 chars>:<uuid>`, e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...`. Relying parties that validate/store `jti` as a UUID (UUID columns, regex validation, replay caches keyed by UUID) will break, and no release note or upgrading guide entry is included in this PR. A user-visible format change of a standard claim needs an explicit documentation entry describing the new format and the fact that older tokens keep the plain-UUID form.
